title: Who's Who: Basil Okoro
summary: Retrieval conservator whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Basil Okoro (born 1840) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a retrieval conservator whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.

Okoro developed sealed cabinets with replaceable witness plates that reveal whether a stored retrieval has influenced its surroundings. He refuses to restore an object to an imagined original state, insisting that every alteration is part of its history.
Museums consult him when an exhibit seems to change between cataloguing and display.

For Alderwick readers, Basil Okoro stands not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
